summary: Registers a Uniform Resource Name namespace identifier for resources published by the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP), the group behind mobile telephony standards. It describes the namespace so 3GPP can name its resources persistently, with the 3GPP Support Team handling management. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: Libraries give every book a permanent call number. This gives the mobile phone standards group its own kind of permanent name for its documents and things, so they can always be found.

subtitle: Permanent names for mobile phone standards documents

tldr.problem: The 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) standards group needs persistent, unique names for the documents and resources it defines.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC registers a URN (Uniform Resource Name) namespace identifier for 3GPP, allowing it to name resources with the prefix urn:3gpp: and manage them through its own procedures.
tldr.outcome: 3GPP can now assign unique, persistent names to its resources that will remain stable even if the organization changes, ensuring reliable reference and discovery.

today: RFC 5279 is an Informational document published in July 2008 and remains the definition of the 3GPP URN namespace, which is still in use for naming 3GPP resources.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
3GPP is a partnership of international telecommunications standards bodies that develops standards for cellular networks. Its members include network operators, equipment vendors, content providers, and other companies in the mobile market.

Many of 3GPP's technologies require persistent names for the documents, specifications, and resources they define. The RFC explains that 3GPP decided to register a formal URN (Uniform Resource Name) namespace to manage these names reliably and persistently.
sections.plainLanguage: The mobile phone standards group needed a permanent name system for all the things it makes, just like how books get library numbers.

sections.title: The 3GPP URN Namespace
sections.content:
The registered namespace identifier is 3gpp. Resources named under this namespace follow the pattern urn:3gpp:{3gpp-urn}, where the part after 3gpp: is an ASCII string following the URN syntax rules defined in RFC 2141.

3GPP itself manages the namespace and controls what strings are assigned. The organization can register its own specifications and services, allow other entities to register sub-trees under the namespace, or permit experimental values in clearly marked sub-namespaces.
sections.plainLanguage: All 3GPP names start with urn:3gpp: followed by what the thing is, like urn:3gpp:featurephones.

sections.title: Example Names
sections.content:
The RFC provides examples of how 3GPP might use the namespace. A name like urn:3gpp:featurephones identifies the 3GPP resource for featurephones. A name like urn:3gpp:acme.foo-serv shows how an operator identified by acme could register its own service foo-serv under the 3GPP namespace.

These examples are illustrative. The actual strings assigned are managed by 3GPP's registration procedures.
sections.plainLanguage: Names might be things like urn:3gpp:featurephones or urn:3gpp:acme.foo-serv, just like how library numbers follow a pattern.

sections.title: How 3GPP Manages the Namespace
sections.content:
3GPP maintains registration tables documenting each assigned name, describing what it is for, which 3GPP spec defines it, and who requested the assignment.

The RFC notes that 3GPP publishes and maintains this information on its website. The organization can handle three types of registration activities: values for 3GPP specs and services, assignments to other organizations, and experimental names used for testing purposes.
sections.plainLanguage: 3GPP keeps a list of all the names it has given out, what each one is for, and where it is defined.

references.text: Daigle, L., van Gulik, D., Iannella, R., and P. Faltstrom, "Uniform Resource Names (URN) Namespace Definition Mechanisms", BCP 66, RFC 3406, October 2002.
